title: Declared test commands: JUnit result reader (P4b), the follow-up to the TRX pilot
outcome: A declared test command whose artifact is JUnit XML (root `testsuites` or `testsuite`) is judged PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN by the P4b rules, on the same declaration and artifact rules as the TRX pilot.
acceptance: P4b JUNIT READER — a SEPARABLE criterion, never a reason to slip TRX. Same declaration, same artifact rules (P1, P3), same scanner style (P4). Dialect is chosen by the root element: `TestRun` = TRX (P4), `testsuites` or `testsuite` = JUnit (P4b); any other root is UNKNOWN "unparsed artifact". JUnit counts: `tests`, `failures`, `errors`, `skipped` read from `<testsuites>` when present, otherwise summed over the `<testsuite>` elements; a mismatch between the two levels, a missing `tests`, or a non-integer is UNKNOWN. Outcome: PASS = exit 0 AND tests − skipped ≥ 1 AND failures = errors = 0; FAIL = exit ≠ 0 OR failures + errors ≥ 1; UNKNOWN otherwise (zero tests, all skipped, unparsed). JUnit has no single schema, so the scanner admits the common shape (Vitest's junit reporter, pytest --junitxml, Maven Surefire, the dotnet JunitXml.TestLogger) and says UNKNOWN for anything else; that is the stated limit, not a gap.

FIXTURES for P4b: real files from a producer at hand without new packages — this repository's own Vitest run with `--reporter=junit` on a tiny spec under `.tmp` (pass, fail, zero) — plus one synthetic malformed file; a dotnet JunitXml.TestLogger capture is welcome but not required.
the live proof gains one step only if P4b landed: a Vitest spec with a declared `--reporter=junit` artifact, pass credited, fail published.
